review::.::holistic::cross_module_archit.summary: sync/file-sync-strategy.ts bypasses vcs/index.ts barrel for FileAction import

evidence: Line 3: import type { FileAction } from "../vcs/types.js" — FileAction is re-exported from src/vcs/index.ts, so this should use ../vcs/index.js to respect the barrel boundary. This is the same class of issue fixed in commit d9904db but was missed.
detail.suggestion: Change line 3 from 'import type { FileAction } from "../vcs/types.js"' to 'import type { FileAction } from "../vcs/index.js"'.

review::.::holistic::convention_outlier:.summary: file-sync-strategy.ts bypasses vcs barrel for FileAction import

evidence: Line 3 imports FileAction from '../vcs/types.js' while FileAction is exported from '../vcs/index.js'. All other cross-module imports in the sync/ directory use barrel imports (../vcs/index.js, ../config/index.js).
detail.suggestion: Change import on line 3 from '../vcs/types.js' to '../vcs/index.js' to match the barrel import convention used by all sibling files.

review::.::holistic::error_consistency::.summary: checkAutoMergeEnabled() swallows permanent auth errors unlike sibling checkExistingPR()

evidence: checkAutoMergeEnabled() (line 200-212) catches all errors and returns false, while checkExistingPR() (line 57-68) in the same class re-throws permanent errors via isPermanentError(). Auth failures during auto-merge check are silently swallowed, hiding credential problems.
detail.suggestion: Add the same isPermanentError() guard used in checkExistingPR(): before the warn+return-false fallback, check if(isPermanentError(error)) throw error. This makes the two sibling methods consistent and surfaces auth problems.

review::.::holistic::error_consistency::.summary: fileExistsOnBranch() catches all git errors as 'not found' unlike sibling methods that discriminate

evidence: fileExistsOnBranch() (line 225-239) catches any error from git show and returns false. In contrast, wouldChange() (line 177-186) and getFileContent() (line 150-156) discriminate ENOENT/EACCES and re-throw unexpected errors. While git CLI errors lack errno codes making exact discrimination harder, the inconsistency within the same class creates different failure semantics for peer methods.
detail.suggestion: Check the error message for expected patterns (e.g., 'does not exist', 'not a tree object', 'exists on disk, but not in') and re-throw others. This aligns with the isRepoNotFoundError pattern used in github-lifecycle-provider.ts for similar git-CLI error discrimination.

review::.::holistic::naming_quality::gen.summary: 'current' parameter name hides its purpose as a 1-based repo progress counter

evidence: In sync-command.ts line 381: 'const current = index + 1' — a developer seeing 'current' passed to logSettingsResult, getLogger().progress(), getLogger().error() etc. cannot tell this is a 1-based progress counter without reading the Logger implementation
In cli/types.ts line 78: ApplyRepoSettingsContext has 'current: number' with no doc comment — reads as 'current what?'
In shared/logger.ts lines 39-42 and 73-114: progress/success/skip/error methods all accept 'current: number' as first param — the Logger is the origin of this naming choice that propagates outward
detail.suggestion: Rename 'current' to 'repoNumber' in Logger.progress/success/skip/error signatures, ApplyRepoSettingsContext, and all call sites in sync-command.ts. This is a mechanical rename across 3 files (~15 call sites).

review::.::holistic::low_level_elegance:.summary: renderLeafNode has 6 interleaved action/complexity branches across 47 lines, impeding scanability

evidence: Lines 200-247: renderLeafNode checks action (add/remove/change) crossed with hasComplexNew/hasComplexOld producing 6 code paths with similar-looking but subtly different line-push logic
detail.suggestion: Extract each action case into its own 10-line helper (renderAddLeaf, renderRemoveLeaf, renderChangeLeaf) that encapsulates the complex-vs-scalar branching internally. This makes the parent switch a 3-way dispatch with no nested conditions.

review::.::holistic::low_level_elegance:.summary: formatRulesetPlan filters changes into 4 groups then repeats structural setup for each group

evidence: Lines 308-311: Four separate .filter() calls on the same array to split by action. Lines 313-316: Four counting assignments that are trivially derivable from the filtered arrays' lengths. The create/update/delete sections then follow an identical loop structure (push header, iterate changes, push entries).
detail.suggestion: Use a single pass to group changes by action into a Map<RulesetAction, RulesetChange[]>, then iterate the map entries. This removes the 4 redundant filter passes and the 4 separate count assignments. The per-action rendering logic stays as-is since each action has different display needs.

review::.::holistic::mid_level_elegance:.summary: SettingsResult in cli/types.ts is a parallel projection of BaseProcessorResult bridged via 'as' cast

evidence: cli/types.ts:62-68 defines SettingsResult with {success, message, skipped?, planOutput?: {lines?: string[]}, warnings?: string[]} which overlaps with but is structurally separate from BaseProcessorResult in settings/base-processor.ts
sync-command.ts:261 bridges the boundary with '.then((result) => result as SettingsResult)' - an implicit contract rather than a structural mapper or shared type
detail.suggestion: Make SettingsResult extend or Pick from BaseProcessorResult to create a single source of truth. For example: 'export type SettingsResult = BaseProcessorResult & { planOutput?: { lines?: string[] }; warnings?: string[] }'. This makes the relationship explicit and lets the compiler catch drift. The 'as' cast in runSettingsProcessor then becomes unnecessary since the return type already satisfies the constraint.

review::.::holistic::test_strategy::proc.summary: repository-processor.test.ts mutates process.env for GitHub App credential tests instead of injecting env

evidence: Lines 1754-1755, 1877-1878, 1955-1956, 2027-2028, 2099-2100 set process.env.XFG_GITHUB_APP_ID and process.env.XFG_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY directly in ~5 test blocks; while cleanup uses try/finally, this creates shared mutable state that would break under parallel test execution
detail.suggestion: Refactor RepositoryProcessor (or its commit strategy selection) to accept an env parameter for credential lookup, matching the DI pattern used elsewhere (e.g. config normalizer accepts env: Record<string, string | undefined>). Tests would then pass a local env object instead of mutating process.env.

review::.::holistic::type_safety::unchec.summary: parseApiJson<T> performs unchecked JSON.parse-as-T on external API responses at 10+ call sites

evidence: parseApiJson<T> at src/shared/json-utils.ts:11 does `JSON.parse(response) as T` with no shape validation
Called with specific types like GitHubRuleset[], CurrentRepoSettings, GitHubLabel[] — if API changes a field name or type, the cast silently produces a mistyped object
10+ call sites across settings strategies and VCS code all rely on this unchecked cast
detail.suggestion: For the most critical response types (GitHubRuleset[], CurrentRepoSettings), add lightweight runtime shape checks after parsing — even just verifying that expected discriminant fields exist (e.g., `if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) throw ...`). This does not require a validation library; targeted checks on the 2-3 highest-risk response types would meaningfully improve safety.

resolution_attestation.text: I have reviewed this triage skip against the code and I am not gaming the score by suppressing a real defect. Standard TypeScript JSON.parse pattern, runtime shape validation would require validation library at 10+ call sites.
